beliefs: f reverses the order of characters in the input [E1, E2, E3]
f swaps the case of each letter (lowercase becomes uppercase, uppercase becomes lowercase) — it does NOT uppercase everything [E1, E2, E3]
The case swap is applied to each character before/independent of the reversal, so a letter's output case is the opposite of its input case [E2, E3]
Non-letter characters (spaces, digits, symbols) are preserved and reversed along with everything else [E1, E3]
Empty string maps to empty string [E1]
notes: E3 shows case is swapped (not uppercased): 'aB'->'Ba', 'AbC'->'Cba'. So the rule is reverse the string and swap the case of each letter, which is equivalent to swapping case then reversing.
